name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Pashhur. His lineage is noted in Nehemiah 11:12, highlighting his priestly heritage. Beyond his paternal connection, there are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'y-h-v-h remembers,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the remembrance by God. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God in the biblical text. The meaning underscores a connection to God's faithfulness and memory.
familyAndRelationships: Zechariah is explicitly identified as the son of Pashhur and is inferred to be the father of Amzi, according to Nehemiah 11:12. These relationships situate him within a priestly family line, confirming his heritage within the tribe of Levi. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies in his role as a Levite priest during the post-exilic period, as evidenced by his identification as the son of Pashhur. His inclusion in Nehemiah 11:12 places him within the restored community of Israel, emphasizing the continuity of the priestly line after the exile. Though brief, his mention affirms God's ongoing covenant faithfulness through the priesthood.
